The "Tip-of-the-Tongue" Phenomenon (Psychology) If you are referring to the frustrating mental block where you know a word or a person's name but cannot quite retrieve it, you are experiencing the tip-of-the-tongue (TOT) phenomenon. ●​ The "Gap": This is a literal processing gap in the brain's lexical retrieval system. Your brain successfully accesses the concept and meaning of the word (semantic memory), but experiences a temporary disconnect when trying to retrieve its specific sound and structure (phonological form). [1] 2. The Gag Reflex (Physiology) If you are looking for an actual physical reflex, you might be thinking of the gag reflex (formally known as the pharyngeal reflex). [1, 2] ●​ The Mechanism: This is an involuntary contraction of the back of the throat triggered by objects touching the soft palate, tongue, or pharynx. Its biological purpose is to protect your airway and prevent choking. [1, 2, 3] 3. Word-Finding Deficits / Anomia (Neurology) In cognitive science and neurology, a persistent or severe difficulty in naming objects or finding words is called anomia or a naming deficit. This is common in conditions like aphasia or early-stage dementia.
